questions.question: Why do speech recognizers need a sequence method in addition to classifying audio frames?
options: Audio frames do not align one-to-one with output tokens
The transcript length is fixed before recording begins
Each audio frame already contains exactly one output word
Silence always marks a word boundary reliably
questions.explanation: Acoustic frames do not map one-to-one to words or characters, and speech durations vary, so the transcript length is not known before decoding. A sequence method must align variable-duration audio evidence with a variable-length token sequence.

questions.question: Greedy CTC sees the best path `t t blank t`. What transcript does collapse-repeats-then-remove-blanks produce?
options: blank t
t
t_t
tt
questions.explanation: Greedy CTC first collapses adjacent repeats: t t blank t becomes t blank t, then blank removal leaves tt. The “t” option would result from deleting blank first, which makes the two remaining t symbols adjacent before collapsing.

questions.question: Which RNN-T component combines encoder-frame information with the token-history predictor state?
options: The blank-removal decoder
The autoregressive cross-attention decoder
The joiner network
The mel filterbank projection
questions.explanation: RNN-T’s joiner combines the encoder’s current audio-frame representation with the predictor’s token-history state to score the next output. Cross-attention belongs to the attention encoder-decoder formulation; RNN-T uses its joiner for the joint distribution.

questions.question: Reference has 5 words; hypothesis has one substitution and one insertion. What is WER?
questions.explanation: WER counts word substitutions, deletions, and insertions over the reference length: (1 + 0 + 1)/5 = 0.40. The 0.33 distractor divides two edits by the six-word hypothesis; WER uses the five reference words.

questions.question: A CTC recognizer is streamable but often misses contextual word choices. What documented addition can help?
options: Use independent argmax decoding with a larger vocabulary
Delay decoding until every frame is converted to mel
Replace its blank token with a punctuation token
Fuse an external language model during beam search
questions.explanation: CTC predicts each frame independently, so an external language model can add sequence-level word context during beam search or shallow fusion. A bigger vocabulary does not change conditional independence, so greedy per-frame choices still lack language context.

questions.question: A 4-minute recording is sent to Whisper. Which handling addresses its documented input-window limit?
options: Use VAD-based chunks with 30-second windows and overlap
Split it into non-overlapping one-second windows
Convert it into a single transcript before inference
Send the complete recording as one unchunked window
questions.explanation: Whisper processes a fixed 30-second window, so a four-minute clip must be divided into bounded chunks, often around speech regions. A single four-minute input exceeds the documented window instead of preserving the full recording through chunking.
